one_line: Personified guardian of Puri’s sacred temple economy and Odisha’s maritime networks, c. 12th–14th century CE.

appearance.age_look: early 30s, lean but sturdy build, height slightly above average
appearance.face: oval face with broad forehead, medium-brown coastal Odia complexion, sharp observant eyes, straight nose, trimmed black moustache and short beard, default expression calm, thoughtful and quietly authoritative
appearance.hair: thick black hair tied in a neat low bun at the nape under a simple off-white cotton turban wrapped flat, with a narrow deep-red band at the edge and a small tilaka in sandalwood paste on the forehead
appearance.costume: He wears a long-sleeved off-white cotton angarakha tunic reaching mid-thigh, overlapping and tied on the right side with visible fabric cords, over a calf-length deep-indigo dhoti wrapped in the Odisha style with a neat front pleat and a thin deep-red border; over his left shoulder is a mustard-yellow cotton uttariya shawl with a subtle woven check pattern, draped diagonally across the chest and back; simple brown leather sandals, a palm-leaf waist pouch tied by cord, a thin gold chain around the neck, and a wooden bead bracelet on the right wrist complete the look.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cotton cord and a small wooden stylus tucked beside it in his left hand, symbolizing temple records and maritime accounts, while his right hand often rests on a small cloth bag of cowries and metal coins at his waist.

ref_desc: A lean early-30s Odia man with an off-white turban, palm-leaf manuscript and stylus, off-white angarakha, deep-indigo dhoti with red border, mustard-yellow shawl, cowrie pouch, and brown sandals in a calm, thoughtful pose using off-white, deep indigo, mustard yellow, deep red, and brown.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style male character embodying the 12th–14th century Jagannath Temple economy of Puri and Odisha’s coastal networks: an early-30s, lean, medium-brown Odia man with an oval face, sharp eyes, trimmed moustache and short beard, wearing thick black hair tied in a low bun under a simple off-white cotton turban edged with a narrow deep-red band and a sandalwood tilaka on his forehead. He is dressed in a long-sleeved off-white cotton angarakha that overlaps and ties on the right, over a calf-length deep-indigo dhoti wrapped in the Odisha style with a neat front pleat and a thin deep-red border. A mustard-yellow cotton uttariya shawl with a subtle woven check pattern is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and back, and he stands in simple brown leather sandals. At his waist sits a small palm-leaf pouch holding cowries and metal coins, and on his right wrist is a wooden bead bracelet with a thin gold chain around his neck. His left hand holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cotton cord, with a small wooden stylus tucked beside it, while his right hand rests lightly on the coin pouch, suggesting his role in managing temple land grants, kitchen supplies, pilgrimage offerings, and coastal trade. Use off-white, deep indigo, mustard yellow, deep red, and brown as the dominant colours, and present him front-facing in a neutral stance so all facial features, hairstyle, garments, and accessories are clearly visible for consistent redrawing.
